entry_conditions: Accept causal world-frame qpos/qvel, TCP/red/blue poses (metres, wxyz), drawer position/velocity and goal fields, with two observation frames. The earliest supported entry still has TCP near [-0.326,0,0.128] m at a moving handle, drawer about 0.1863 m with velocity 0.1071 m/s, and fingers about 0.00707 and 0.00705 m each (total 0.01413 m). Do not equate that narrow opening with a red grasp. Later supported entries have released fingers near 0.040 m each and TCP near z=0.369 m, or red close to and moving with TCP at z around 0.143 m with fingers near 0.01825 m each. Current drawer opening, finger state, relative TCP/object geometry and causal motion identify which opening/release/retreat/acquisition prerequisites remain. These are measured reference states, not hard rejection thresholds.
exit_conditions: A red-placement exit should check red fully on the pad using the completion geometry, rather than only horizontally over it: overlap starts with red around z=0.211 m, then release brings it to about 0.020 m. Red on the pad alone does not imply the hand has retreated or blue is acquired. Continue through open-finger retreat toward TCP z around 0.300 m and blue pickup if useful. The expanded late endpoint is during blue lift: measured terminal TCP z is about 0.139-0.145 m, blue moves near it, total finger opening is about 0.03648 m and joint velocities are nonzero; do not force a static high waypoint or zero-velocity boundary. These are skill transfer cues only. If the supplied full task completion contract already holds, no extra release, clearance or settling hold is required.
overlap_role: The unchanged incoming shared slices cover original index 195 through stops 474-476, so this policy learns remaining opening, handle release/retreat, red approach, closing and initial lift, not just held-object transport. The outgoing overlap starts at 575, 581 or 582 and continues through assigned stops 845-859, covering red descent/release/retreat and blue approach/grasp/lift. Both ends are chains of physical transitions. The learned event-conditioned spatial intent is refreshed from causal observations and supports local resumption inside these chains; no original index or private phase clock is an input.
successor_readiness: Pass the actual current observations and recent history, including qvel, drawer motion, both finger positions, TCP/object poses and goals. No learned latent or advisory waypoint is required by the successor interface. An early insert_blue takeover must still finish red placement from z approximately 0.211 m, release/retreat and acquire blue. A late takeover should preserve the observed closed-gripper blue lift (demonstrated g=-1), blue/TCP co-motion and nonzero lift velocity, and then continue insertion. Drawer is typically near 0.297 m and red near pad z=0.020 m at late exits. Finger width and proximity only suggest grasp; accompanying object motion is stronger evidence, not a contact guarantee.
failure_signatures: A predicted waypoint or executed trajectory crosses the drawer rim while red remains low; the hand moves laterally before red release/retreat; finger closure is followed by TCP lift without corresponding object motion; red remains above or outside the pad despite a release intent; blue remains at table height while the hand climbs; or a stale intent is pursued despite unchanged object state. Advancing merely because predicted duration elapsed is premature transfer. These are inspection cues, not proven automatic recovery triggers or implemented hard constraints.
continuation_guidance: Continue this model while unfinished transitions remain within its supported expanded slice, especially descending red, opening fingers near placement, retreating vertically, approaching blue or beginning blue lift. Use the full state and two-frame motion to distinguish descending held red from rising empty TCP and rising held blue. An insertion policy may take over earlier in the shared suffix only if it is prepared to finish the remaining red chain. Prefer transfer by the demonstrated initial-blue-lift endpoint rather than asking this model to extrapolate through untrained insertion. Deployment predicts both hierarchy levels from the new history at each replanning call; it has no autonomous event clock or waypoint-based termination hook. Duration/censor predictions are internal conditioning, not a command to the API to switch.
limitations: Observed training support does not certify policy success, safe clearance, grasp/contact or recovery after disturbances. The hierarchy is supervised by local future states within 16 slots; absent semantic changes are censored and complete distant high waypoints are not available as labels. Event labels are geometric proxies. The waypoint diffusion uses a deterministic central inference path; action diffusion remains the fixed learned DDPM. No IK, collision geometry, external planner, script, image encoder, joint-action equivariance or compulsory private handoff code exists. The separate global completion rule requires only simultaneous drawer-open, red-on-pad and blue-inside spatial predicates, not additional release or sustained stability.
